To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the effects of dietary marine and freshwater fish oils on plasma and liver lipid profiles of rats depend on the composition of their n−3 poly-unsaturated fatty acids, and that the hypoliplipdemic effect of fish oils depends on the composition rather than on the amount of n−3 polyunsturated fatty acids.
the hypolidemic effects of fish oil are not only due to its n−3 PUFA composition but also to the relative proportions of the n−6 PUFA to n−3 PUFAs.
the dietary fish oils with similar total levels of n−3 poly unsaturated fatty acids but different EPA and AA compositions have different effects on plasma and liver lipid profiles in rats.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of fish oils with different fatty acid compositions on the plasma lipid profile of rats.
the effects of dietary oils on the plasma and hepatic lipid profiles.
the effects of fish oil on the plasma lipid profiles in rat fed on a diet supplemented with either marine or fresh water fish oil for 60 days.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
EPA-rich fish oils exert hypolipidemia in the rat model.
the hypolipedemic effects of fish oils are dependent on the EPA/AA ratio in the diet and not on the absolute amount of EPA in the diet.
EPA is more effective than AA in reducing plasma triacylglycerols and phospholipids and in lowering cholesterol levels.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the n−3 PUFA in fish oils are beneficial to human health but the composition of the fatty acids in the fish oils is important.
the EPA to AA ratio in the diet is an important determinant of the lipid profile of the animal.
the n−3 fatty acid composition of the dietary fish oils is more important than the n−3 content in determining their effect on lipid levels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the n−3 fatty acid composition of the diet is more important than the quantity of the diet in influencing the plasma lipid profile.
the hypoliepidemic effect of fish oil depends on its composition rather than the total amount of n-3 polyunsaturated acids.
fish oil rich in EPA, but not in ALA, is more effective in lowering serum lipid levels.
